q: On the cover of the Beatles' 1969 album Abbey Road, what are the four members doing?
note: The London crossing was given protected landmark status in 2010.

q: What is the name of the Memphis mansion where Elvis Presley lived and is buried?
note: He bought it in 1957, when he was only 22 years old.

q: What is the title of Michael Jackson's 1982 album whose title track ends with a spoken passage by horror star Vincent Price?
note: Quincy Jones produced it, and its videos helped break the color barrier on early MTV.

q: Which Queen song from 1975 opens with the line 'Is this the real life? Is this just fantasy?'
note: It runs close to six minutes, which radio programmers insisted was far too long for a single.

q: Which band's 1991 single 'Smells Like Teen Spirit' pushed grunge into the mainstream?
note: Kurt Cobain took the title from a friend's graffiti, not realizing it named a brand of deodorant.

q: Which Swedish group won the 1974 Eurovision Song Contest with the song 'Waterloo'?
note: The name is an acronym built from the four members' first names.

q: Which 1973 Pink Floyd album has a prism splitting white light into a rainbow on its cover?
a: The Dark Side of the Moon
note: The sleeve was designed by the art studio Hipgnosis and carries almost no text at all.

q: Which American songwriter was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2016?
note: He took weeks to acknowledge the prize and then skipped the ceremony altogether.

q: Which singer turned Otis Redding's song 'Respect' into a 1967 anthem?
note: Her version added the spelled-out chorus and the 'sock it to me' backing vocals sung by her sisters.

q: Which Buggles song was the first music video played on MTV in 1981?
note: MTV launched on August 1, 1981, and at first reached only a slice of New Jersey cable subscribers.

q: Whitney Houston's 1992 recording of 'I Will Always Love You' was written by which country singer?
note: Parton took her own version to number one on the country chart back in 1974.

q: Which band recorded the 1977 album Rumours while its couples were breaking up?
note: Two romances inside the band collapsed during the sessions, and the fallout became the songs.

q: What was the title of the Sugarhill Gang's 1979 single that first carried hip-hop onto mainstream radio?
note: Its backing track lifts the groove from Chic's disco hit 'Good Times.'

q: What was the name of the 1985 charity concert staged simultaneously at Wembley Stadium and Philadelphia's JFK Stadium?
note: Bob Geldof organized it to raise money for famine relief in Ethiopia.

q: Which musician starred in and wrote the songs for the 1984 film Purple Rain?
note: He won an Academy Award for the film's music.

q: Taylor Swift's 2014 album 1989 takes its title from what?
note: The record marked her deliberate move from country music to pop.

q: Under what name was the singer Elton John born?
note: He borrowed the 'John' from Long John Baldry, a singer he played alongside in his early years.

q: The 1969 Woodstock music festival was held on a dairy farm in which US state?
note: It took place on Max Yasgur's land near Bethel, not in the town of Woodstock at all.

q: Which Detroit record label, founded by Berry Gordy in 1959, launched the Supremes and the Temptations?
note: Its modest headquarters carried a sign reading Hitsville U.S.A.

q: What was the name of the flame-haired alien rock star alter ego David Bowie adopted for his 1972 album?
note: Bowie killed the character off from the stage in 1973, blindsiding both his fans and his own band.
